Alright, let me think through this year's plan...

---

*Speaking as the farmer:*

I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation for nearly 30 years now, so most of it is routine. With 50 mu that's a decent-sized farm around here — bigger than most of my neighbors who only have 10-20 mu. My wife and I do most of the field work, my oldest son helps when he's back from the city, and we hire people for harvest and planting when the turnaround between wheat and maize gets tight.

**For the wheat this year:** I'll plant around October 10th like always, using the Jimai variety I used last year — it did fine, about 480 kg/mu. I buy seed from the agricultural supply store, don't save my own anymore because the yields drop. Before planting I'll put down compound fertilizer as base, maybe 40 kg/mu of the 15-15-15 stuff, plus some urea. Then at jointing in March I'll topdress another 15-20 kg of urea per mu if the wheat looks a bit yellow. The extension guy told us 15 kg N/mu is enough but honestly I do a bit more, around 17-18 kg N total — I'd rather spend the extra hundred yuan than have a weak crop. Water: I'll irrigate at overwintering in November, then jointing, then grain filling — three times usually, four if spring is dry. Pumping costs money so I don't water more than I need.

**For the maize:** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June I have maybe 5-7 days to get maize in the ground. I use a no-till planter that the village cooperative rents out — saves me 2-3 days and that matters. Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, about 4 kg/mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage in late July. Maize here gets enough summer rain usually so I only irrigate once or twice if it turns dry in August. Should get around 500 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Pesticides:** I spray herbicide on wheat in early spring for weeds, and I watch for aphids — if I see them bad I spray, otherwise I don't bother. Maize gets a pre-emergent herbicide and usually one spray for corn borer.

**Labor:** My wife and I can handle most of the fieldwork across 50 mu because I use the cooperative's machinery for tillage, planting, and harvest. I hire 2-3 people for maybe 10-15 days total during the wheat-maize turnaround and final harvests. My son sometimes comes back for harvest week.

**Budget:** Last year I spent maybe 650 yuan per mu total on inputs across both crops. I keep some cash reserve because you never know — equipment breakdowns, or a bad year.
